exceptions.responsibility: Art runtime settings validation, credential binding, version selection, and accessible dialog focus lifecycle
exceptions.reason: The dialog remains a single atomic form because its validation and secret-binding state must be submitted together; it is below the 700-line soft cap after the App extraction.

exceptions.responsibility: Installed Art lifecycle, authoring submission, MCP dependency credentials, and registry refresh coordination
exceptions.reason: The coordinator keeps mutation and refresh ordering in one ownership boundary; dialogs and wizard UI are already separate and the remaining file is below the 700-line soft cap.

exceptions.responsibility: Art wizard state transitions, source discovery, workflow inference, MCP discovery, and submission assembly
exceptions.reason: The presentation layer is separate; the remaining controller preserves cross-mode reset and inference ordering as one hook and only narrowly exceeds the 500-line preferred size.

exceptions.responsibility: Accessible Loom and Hook settings page composition, shortcut editors, and quick-binding dialogs
exceptions.reason: State and side effects are already isolated in a controller hook; the attached tab and portal markup remains together to preserve its ARIA and focus contracts.

exceptions.responsibility: Settings hydration, ordered autosave, runtime application, cache operations, diagnostics, and shortcut conflict state
exceptions.reason: The view and application-link actions are separate, but autosave rollback and runtime/cache application share ordering-sensitive refs; the cohesive controller remains below the 700-line soft cap pending focused state-machine tests.

exceptions.responsibility: Untrusted image-search MCP candidate normalization, provenance tracking, SSRF-safe bounded downloads, thumbnail fallback, and canonical runtime output
exceptions.reason: The recursive candidate walk and redirect-aware downloader share script-scoped depth, candidate, redirect, MIME, address-policy, and size limits; extracting either side without a new tested module API would split one security boundary and risk inconsistent provenance or SSRF decisions.

exceptions.responsibility: Shared image runtime path confinement, bounded data decoding, GDI+ lifetime, bitmap transforms, thumbnail generation, and protocol response assembly
exceptions.reason: These helpers form one copied runtime kernel whose allowed-root, size, file-identity, disposal, and output-shape invariants are reused together; a further split would add fragile import ordering or duplicate the security policy across packaged Arts.

exceptions.responsibility: The complete loom.hook.v1 wire contract: method namespace, negotiation, transports, typed requests, responses, events, and validation
exceptions.reason: Method constants, serde tags, payload types, transport capabilities, and handshake validation are one versioned protocol surface; splitting by request or response direction would scatter wire-shape invariants and create cross-module public coupling for a file still below the soft cap.

exceptions.responsibility: Workflow graph validation and ordering, durable executor event sequencing, Hook dispatch, run summaries, and SystemOne/SystemTwo public facades
exceptions.reason: The executor consumes graph validation and ordering as one transaction, from run_started through per-node Hook events to run_finished; keeping that invariant local avoids exposing private ordering details across modules, and the thin public facades leave the cohesive implementation only narrowly above 500 lines.

exceptions.responsibility: One isolated Gateway planner transaction from fixture and daemon startup through HTTP capture, run persistence, secret checks, and cleanup
exceptions.reason: The temporary ports, Gateway job, daemon token, planner configuration, captured request, and persisted run ID must remain in one lifecycle to prove causality and token non-disclosure; splitting would turn the semantic end-to-end assertion into disconnected process checks.

exceptions.responsibility: Packaged Loom desktop, daemon, Hook Bridge, CDP, fixture revision, UI refresh, and process-lifetime end-to-end verification
exceptions.reason: Initial and updated Hook revisions must be correlated across one live desktop-daemon-bridge-CDP session, and the same process ownership is required for leak detection; splitting would sever the 3-node to 4-node fixture mutation from its API and UI evidence.

exceptions.responsibility: Third-party framework and Art compilation, install, Hook execution, upgrade, enablement, restart, removal, source-integrity evidence, and cleanup
exceptions.reason: Every transition reuses the same package identities, control-plane state, upgraded runtime, Hook request, and source fingerprints; keeping the ordered lifecycle together is necessary to prove boundary behavior across restart and reinstall rather than as unrelated fixture tests.

exceptions.responsibility: One SQLite run/event persistence scenario across daemon restart, packaged CLI, optional desktop sibling reuse, PID lineage, and cleanup
exceptions.reason: Daemon A, daemon B, and the desktop sibling must share the same database and run ID so exact event equality and process lineage remain attributable to one restart lifecycle; splitting would destroy that cross-process persistence proof.
